dihydroxyvitamin D [1,25(OH)2D](Fig. 3) (Hossein-nezhad and Holick, 2013).
Neither vitamin D2 nor vitamin D3 possess any intrinsic biologic activity on calcium metabolism. They both require a hydrox-
ylation on carbon 25 to form 25(OH)D (Fig. 4). When given as a 1000 or 2000 IU supplement, vitamin D2 is as effective as vitamin
D3 in raising serum 25(OH)D levels. 25(OH)D is the major circulating form of vitamin D, and at physiologic concentrations, it too
has little biologic activity on calcium metabolism. It must undergo a hydroxylation on carbon 1 in the kidney to form 1,25(OH)2D,
the biologically active form of vitamin D (Fig. 3). The metabolism of 25(OH)D to 1,25(OH)2D is tightly regulated by parathyroid
hormone (PTH), ﬁbroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23), and serum phosphorus levels (Fig. 5). PTH and low serum phosphorus levels
increase the production of 1,25(OH)2D, whereas FGF23 suppresses its production (DeLuca, 1988; Holick, 2007; Hossein-nezhad
and Holick, 2013; Charoenngam et al., 2021).
